ready1_open_rewrite.title: GeoSQA Open-ended Question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The ancient Greek mathematician Eratosthenes came up with a clever idea to measure the circumference of the Earth. Eratosthenes lived in Alexandria, and 785 kilometers due south of this city, there was a city Syene on the same meridian (30°E) as Alexandria. At 12 noon on the summer solstice, while sunlight shone directly to the bottom of a dry well in the city of Syene, Eratosthenes used a wooden pole and a protractor in Alexandria to accurately calculate the circumference of the Earth (∠1 in the figure is 7.2°). Combining the diagram <image1>, what is the relationship between the solar directions seen at place E and Alexandria at this moment?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: At this moment, the solar directions seen at place E and Alexandria are opposite

raw_record.original_question: 古希腊数学家埃拉托斯芬想出一个巧妙的主意来测量地球的周长。埃拉托斯芬生活在亚历山大城，在这座城市正南785千米处，有一座和亚历山大城同在一条子午线（30°E）上的城市塞尼。夏至日正午12点，阳光直射塞尼城中一口枯井底部的同时，埃拉托斯芬在亚历山大城使用木竿和量角器精确计算出了地球的周长（图中∠1为7.2°）。结合图示<image1>，此刻E地和亚历山大城所看到的太阳方位有什么关系？
raw_record.answer: At this moment, the solar directions seen at place E and Alexandria are opposite
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure the Earth is a circular cross-section, with multiple parallel sunlight rays on the right side shining toward the Earth; Alexandria and Syene are both marked near the same illuminated hemisphere on the right side of the Earth, with Syene south of Alexandria; point E is marked in the upper-left part of the Earth at a high-latitude position in the Northern Hemisphere, close to one side of the terminator in the figure.
Then reason: The stem explains that at 12 noon on the summer solstice, the Sun is directly over Syene, and Syene and Alexandria are on the same 30°E meridian, with Syene located due south of Alexandria. Therefore at this moment Alexandria is also at local noon, and Alexandria is located north of the direct solar point, so Alexandria sees the Sun in the due south direction. Combining the fact that point E in the figure is located at high latitude in the Northern Hemisphere and near the terminator opposite to the noon side of Alexandria, it can be judged that place E at this moment sees the Sun near the north. Thus the solar directions seen at the two places are one toward south and one toward north, with opposite directions.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The ancient Greek mathematician Eratosthenes came up with a clever idea to measure the circumference of the Earth. Eratosthenes lived in Alexandria, and 785 kilometers due south of this city, there was a city Syene on the same meridian (30°E) as Alexandria. At 12 noon on the summer solstice, while sunlight shone directly to the bottom of a dry well in the city of Syene, Eratosthenes used a wooden pole and a protractor in Alexandria to accurately calculate the circumference of the Earth (∠1 in the figure is 7.2°). Combining the diagram <image1>, what is the relationship between the solar directions seen at place E and Alexandria at this moment?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: At this moment, the solar directions seen at place E and Alexandria are opposite
